title: Colgate-Palmolive vs. lululemon athletica: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:

Sara Appino, The Motley Fool

LULU

Choosing between a steady staples giant and a premium apparel leader requires balancing reliability against growth potential. Investors must decide if Colgate-Palmolive (NYSE:CL) or lululemon athletica (NASDAQ:LULU) better suits their 2027 goals.

Colgate-Palmolive dominates everyday essentials like toothpaste and pet nutrition, while Lululemon leads the premium athletic wear market. One offers defensive qualities in volatile markets, and the other aims for expansion in international retail. This comparison looks at their growth paths, financial health, and current valuations to help you navigate these two distinct paths.

The case for Colgate-Palmolive

Colgate-Palmolive reaches consumers in more than 200 countries with a diverse portfolio including oral care, home hygiene, and specialty pet nutrition. In its latest annual report, Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) and its affiliates accounted for nearly 11% of total net sales. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk, though the company continues to expand its presence in emerging markets among consumer staples stocks.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $21.3 billion, reflecting a growth rate of roughly 5.9%. Net income for the same period was close to $2.1 billion, resulting in a net margin of nearly 9.6%. These results indicate a consistent demand for hygiene and pet health products despite broader economic shifts.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached approximately 158.4x, which represents the relationship between its total debt and shareholder equity. The current ratio, measuring the ability to pay short-term debts with current assets, was roughly 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $3.6 billion.

The case for lululemon athletica

Lululemon Athletica operates a premium athletic lifestyle business focused on technical apparel, footwear, and accessories. The company uses an omni-channel approach, selling through over 800 stores and its own digital platforms. The company also uses license and supply arrangements with third parties to enter international markets like the UAE and Israel.

In the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached nearly $11.1 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 1.7%. Net income for this period was roughly $1.4 billion, resulting in a net margin of nearly 12.8%. The slower revenue growth suggests a period of normalization following years of rapid post-pandemic expansion.

As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.4x, showing the company uses relatively little debt compared to its equity. The current ratio was approximately 2.3x, suggesting a strong ability to cover short-term obligations. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow reached close to $921.7 million.

Today's big story: Will 2027 Be A 2022 Repeat For Stocks?

Walmart (WMT) did better than expected on Thursday, and its stock still fell. Revenue for the quarter to October grew 4.5% in constant currency. Constant currency means before the effect of exchange rates. That was 0.75 points above the top of the range Walmart gave in August, though that range covered net sales only. Earnings and revenue also came in just above analysts' expectations. The shares closed down 1.0% at $126.04.

Walmart's growth story now rests on its online and advertising businesses. Its online sales grew 17% and its advertising business grew 25%. This article asks whether Walmart's cash backs the price investors pay for that story.

Walmart trades at 46.2 times last year's earnings per share. That is below Costco Wholesale at 52.7 and above Amazon.com at 35.9. Yet Walmart kept only 2.09 cents of each dollar of sales as free cash flow last year. Its free cash flow per dollar of sales has been below its 10-year median of 2.55 cents in each of the last five years.

Did Walmart fall because of its report or because of the market?

The whole market fell on Thursday. SPY, a fund that tracks the S&P 500, dropped 2.0%. Walmart fell 0.93 points less than SPY, so the market explains more of the day than the report does. Walmart had also fallen on each of its three report days before this one.

Walmart dropped 9.2% on its August report day, and it slipped again this time despite a beat. If Walmart is a big part of your savings, drops like that are hard to sit through, good news or not. When the market has fallen, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has lost about 81 cents for every $1 its benchmark lost, on average. See the HQ record.

Other retailers had a mixed day. Target rose 0.92%, while Kroger fell 1.6%.

Where did Walmart beat its own plan?

Quarterly revenue was $188.8 billion, up 5.2% as reported. In August, Walmart had guided to net sales growth in a range that topped out at 3.75% in constant currency. The two are close but not identical. The release headline counts total revenue, which includes membership fees. The guidance counted net sales only. Walmart also raised its full-year sales and earnings outlook.

Three parts of the business grew much faster than total revenue:

Online sales grew 17% worldwide.

Advertising grew 25% worldwide.

Membership fee revenue grew 17%.

Is Walmart Stock Too Expensive to Buy Now?

Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) is no longer your grandfather's supermarket chain. The company has evolved. Its financials now include contributions from online sales, advertising, and subscriptions. Shares have soared 162% in the past five years (as of Nov. 16).

The business is valued at $1 trillion. Is this top retail stock too expensive to buy right now?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Walmart's size hasn't gotten in the way of its strong fundamental performance. Net income went from $13.7 billion in fiscal 2021 to $22.3 billion in fiscal 2026, growing 63% over that five-year stretch. This financial metric has been an important tailwind propelling the stock to market-thumping returns.

The valuation, however, is not appealing to new investors. The company can be purchased today at a price-to-earnings ratio of 46.5. You can buy exposure to the S&P 500 index at a 23.3 multiple. And leading artificial intelligence stocks trade at much cheaper valuations.

According to the sell-side analyst community, Walmart's earnings per share will increase at a compound annual rate of 11.1% from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2029. That kind of growth doesn't justify the valuation, even though this is a competitively advantaged business that has long dominated its industry.

In the coming five or 10 years, I think there's a much higher likelihood that the P/E ratio compresses than expands. This introduces greater downside risk, even if Walmart keeps performing well from a fundamental perspective.

Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) slipped 1.04% to $126.04 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 19 after third-quarter results beat on revenue and adjusted earnings. Shares had traded about 1.9% lower before the open, and the retailer finished well below its $135.16 52-week high.

WMT GF Value chart

The quarter was strong. Revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8 billion, ahead of the $187.38 billion estimate, and adjusted EPS of $0.65 beat by a cent. U.S. e-commerce grew 23%, global advertising 25% and membership fee revenue 17%. Walmart lifted full-year constant-currency sales growth to 4.9% to 5.2% from 4.0% to 5.0%, and adjusted EPS to $2.84 to $2.89 from $2.80 to $2.87. The catch is more than $2 billion of incremental costs this year and capex rising to about 4% of net sales.

At the guided EPS midpoint, Walmart trades at about 44 times earnings. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 85/100, a profile of steady profitability, sound finances and strong momentum that has carried the shares higher all year. GF Value is $107.05, so the close sits 17.7% above it, which GuruFocus rates modestly overvalued. Premium quality, premium price. The holiday quarter must prove the higher-margin ad and membership mix can absorb pharmacy deflation and rising costs.

title: Walmart's value proposition supports further market share gains, says Bank of America
detail:
Walmart's value proposition supports further market share gains, says Bank of America
Proactive
Fri, November 20, 2026 at 11:00 AM MST 2 min read
WMT
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart Inc (NYSE:WMT, XETRA:WMT) is positioned to gain further market share through its strengthening value, convenience and product assortment, according to Bank of America (BofA), which reiterated its 'buy' rating and raised its price objective to $141 from $139.

The bank said the retailer continued to gain share across product categories and income groups, led by higher-income households, while management described consumers as stable and resilient.

BofA expects the momentum to continue through the holiday season and beyond, despite an anticipated headwind from Health and Wellness pricing, which could reduce US comparable sales growth by approximately 125 to 150 basis points.

The analyst expects grocery inflation to accelerate from 1.4% in the latest quarter to the mid-2% range during 2027, assuming oil and commodity costs remain elevated.

Walmart's price rollbacks ended the third quarter at approximately 7,700, down from more than 11,000 in the second quarter but still above the historical range of 5,000 to 5,500, helping the retailer achieve some of its strongest food market share gains in three years.

Learn more about Walmart

Read more about Walmart

Walmart+ membership also expanded at a double-digit rate in the first few weeks after the Sam's Club Plus bundle launch, while bundled members increased their online Walmart spending by more than 80% compared with pre-launch levels.

The bank highlighted advertising and marketplace operations as additional growth engines, with US advertising revenue rising 37% and marketplace sales increasing 49%.

VIZIO's expanding installed base and integration of Vibe offer further advertising opportunities, while its television operating system powered the best-selling TV models in the US, with unit volumes rising nearly 150% year on year.

For fiscal 2028, the bank forecasts net sales growth of 4.8% and operating income growth of 8.3%, raising its earnings estimates to $3.20 per share.
